description: This bar chart, from the paper “Mapping the Minds of LLMs: A Graph-Based Analysis of Reasoning LLM,” illustrates the comparison between “Incorrect” and “Correct” reasoning outcomes across five discrete categories labeled 0 through 4 on the horizontal axis. The vertical axis represents the value of γ/B, scaled linearly from 0.0 to 0.6, with tick marks and dashed grid lines at intervals of 0.2. The legend indicates that blue bars with a dotted pattern represent “Incorrect” outcomes, while magenta bars with diagonal hatching represent “Correct” outcomes. For each category on the x-axis, there are two adjacent bars: the “Incorrect” bar is consistently shorter than the “Correct” bar. Specifically, the “Incorrect” bars have approximate values of 0.40 at category 0, 0.40 at category 1, 0.36 at category 2, 0.32 at category 3, and 0.30 at category 4. The corresponding “Correct” bars are significantly taller, with approximate values of 0.70 at category 0, 0.68 at category 1, 0.66 at category 2, 0.64 at category 3, and 0.46 at category 4. The bars are presented in a grouped format, with no apparent sorting order other than the natural sequence of the categories. There are no visual emphasis elements such as shading, bolding, or annotations on any of the bars.
